name: Ben-Ammi
title: Ancestor of the Ammonites
summary: Ben-Ammi was the son of Lot and his youngest daughter, conceived after the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah. His name means 'son of my people', and he became the ancestor of the Ammonites, a people who were often in conflict with Israel throughout Old Testament history.

keyEvents.title: The Destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah
keyEvents.description: God destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah because of their sin, but Lot and his two daughters were saved by fleeing to the mountains.

keyEvents.title: Lot and His Daughters Flee to a Cave
keyEvents.description: After the destruction, Lot settled with his two daughters in a cave in the mountains, as they were afraid to live in Zoar.

keyEvents.title: The Daughters' Plan
keyEvents.description: Lot's daughters, believing there were no other men left, devised a plan to have children by their father by getting him drunk so that they could preserve their family line.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Ben-Ammi
keyEvents.description: The youngest daughter bore a son and named him Ben-Ammi, which means 'son of my people'. He became the ancestor of the Ammonites.

keyEvents.title: The Ammonites as Israel's neighboring people
keyEvents.description: Ben-Ammi's descendants, the Ammonites, became a significant nation east of the Jordan. God forbade Israel to take their land because it was given to Lot's descendants.

keyEvents.title: The relationship between the Ammonites and Israel throughout history
keyEvents.description: The Ammonites were repeatedly in conflict with Israel, including during the time of the judges and the monarchy, and were described by the prophets as a people under God's judgment.
